items.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I used to play [freeze] John Coltrane, Chick Corea, if I can see that on a video I’m going to be one of the happiest men in the world.

ctx.x: Well first of all I was looking for freedom. In my case in particular my life in Cuba was unbearable. I never liked the system, just because the reason that I was not, I disagreed with the system that was against four guys from Liverpool with long hair and tight pants, three guitars and a drum. I didn’t know the message that they were conveying at that time because my English when I arrived into the United States, my English was zero. I had no club about English language. So I don’t know that what they were…

leave the island. Because I knew my future wasn’t in the country where I would not be allowed to express myself musically speaking. Let’s put politics aside, musically speaking. So I always, my dream was always coming to the United States because the music that I wanted to play and my heroes were here. I think that in our previous interview I said that my ultimate dream when I was in Cuba after I became a musician and I knew that jazz was the music that I wanted to play, my ultimate dreams was watching my heroes…
Well you certainly did better than that.
